## Weekly Household Income

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Household weekly income
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
household <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Income_Household.csv",
                               variable = "income") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!income %in% c("Partial income stated", "All incomes not stated", "Not applicable")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(income = dplyr::case_when(
    income == "$3,500 or more ($182,000 or more)" ~ "More than 3000",
    income == "$3,000-$3,499 ($156,000-$181,999)" ~ "More than 3000",
    income == "$2,500-$2,999 ($130,000-$155,999)" ~ "1500 to 2999",
    income == "$2,000-$2,499 ($104,000-$129,999)" ~ "1500 to 2999",
    income == "$1,750-$1,999 ($91,000-$103,999)"  ~ "1500 to 2999",
    income == "$1,500-$1,749 ($78,000-$90,999)"   ~ "1500 to 2999",
    income == "$1,250-$1,499 ($65,000-$77,999)"   ~ "500 to 1499",
    income == "$1,000-$1,249 ($52,000-$64,999)"   ~ "500 to 1499",
    income == "$800-$999 ($41,600-$51,999)"       ~ "500 to 1499",
    income == "$650-$799 ($33,800-$41,599)"       ~ "500 to 1499",
    income == "$500-$649 ($26,000-$33,799)"       ~ "500 to 1499",
    income == "$400-$499 ($20,800-$25,999)"       ~ "Less than 499",
    income == "$300-$399 ($15,600-$20,799)"       ~ "Less than 499",
    income == "$150-$299 ($7,800-$15,599)"        ~ "Less than 499",
    income == "$1-$149 ($1-$7,799)"               ~ "Less than 499",
    income == "Nil income"                        ~ "Less than 499",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# Data wrangling
household_lga <- household %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = income,
                       level    = "household",
                       dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(more_3000_prop = aboriginal_n_more_than_3000 / aboriginal_total * 100,
                more_1500_prop = aboriginal_n_1500_to_2999 / aboriginal_total * 100,
                more_500_prop  = aboriginal_n_500_to_1499 / aboriginal_total * 100,
                less_500_prop  = aboriginal_n_less_than_499 / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                more_3000_n = aboriginal_n_more_than_3000,
                more_3000_prop,
                more_1500_n = aboriginal_n_1500_to_2999,
                more_1500_prop,
                more_500_n = aboriginal_n_500_to_1499,
                more_500_prop,
                less_500_n = aboriginal_n_less_than_499,
                less_500_prop,
                aboriginal_total)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 28% (n = 1,683) of households in the NEPHU catchment with at least one member who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census had a weekly household income of more than \$1,500. This was lower than for non-Indigenous households where 35% had a weekly income of more than \$1,500.

- The number of households in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment with at least one member who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander with a weekly income of less than \$500 ranged from 209 (Darebin LGA) to 18 (Nillumbik LGAs).

- The percentage of households in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment with at least one member who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander with a weekly income of less than \$500 ranged from 26% (Darebin LGA) to 10% (Boroondara and Nillumbik LGAs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the ABS Census 2021. Responses for each household member were summed to calculate the total weekly household income.

- What is the total of all income the person usually receives?
  - Free text response

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Income Support Payments

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Type of income support, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
benefit_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Income_Benefit_LGA.csv",
                                 variable = "benefit") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!benefit %in% c("Not applicable",
                                "Type of benefit unknown", 
                                "Did not receive government pension or allowance", 
                                "Admin not available",
                                "Nil or negative income")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(benefit = dplyr::case_when(
    benefit == "Carer Allowance" ~ "Carer support",
    benefit == "Carer Payment"   ~ "Carer support",
    #
    benefit == "Disability Support Pension" ~ "Disability support",
    benefit == "Mobility Allowance"         ~ "Disability support",
    #
    benefit == "Dad and Partner Pay"         ~ "Family and parenting",
    benefit == "Family Tax Benefits"         ~ "Family and parenting",
    benefit == "Paid Parental Leave Payment" ~ "Family and parenting",
    benefit == "Parenting Payment"           ~ "Family and parenting",
    #
    benefit == "Age Pension"     ~ "Older Australians",
    benefit == "Widow Allowance" ~ "Older Australians",
    #
    benefit == "Austudy/Abstudy"                  ~ "Work and study",
    benefit == "Newstart Allowance and Jobseeker" ~ "Work and study",
    benefit == "Youth Allowance"                  ~ "Work and study",
    #
    benefit == "Future Flexible Support Payment"          ~ "Other payments",
    benefit == "Special Benefit"                          ~ "Other payments",
    benefit == "Other government pensions and allowances" ~ "Other payments",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))  

# Data wrangling
benefit_lga <- benefit_lga %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = benefit,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(carer_prop      = aboriginal_n_carer_support / aboriginal_total * 100,
                disability_prop = aboriginal_n_disability_support / aboriginal_total * 100,
                family_prop     = aboriginal_n_family_and_parenting / aboriginal_total * 100,
                older_prop      = aboriginal_n_older_australians / aboriginal_total * 100,
                study_prop      = aboriginal_n_work_and_study / aboriginal_total * 100,
                other_prop      = aboriginal_n_other_payments / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                carer_n = aboriginal_n_carer_support,
                carer_prop,
                disability_n = aboriginal_n_disability_support,
                disability_prop,
                family_n = aboriginal_n_family_and_parenting,
                family_prop,
                older_n = aboriginal_n_older_australians,
                older_prop,
                study_n = aboriginal_n_work_and_study,
                study_prop,
                other_n = aboriginal_n_other_payments,
                other_prop,
                aboriginal_total)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Type of income support, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
benefit_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Income_Benefit_AgeSex.csv",
                                       variable = "benefit") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!benefit %in% c("Not applicable",
                                "Type of benefit unknown", 
                                "Did not receive government pension or allowance", 
                                "Admin not available",
                                "Nil or negative income")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(benefit = dplyr::case_when(
    benefit == "Carer Allowance" ~ "Carer support",
    benefit == "Carer Payment"   ~ "Carer support",
    #
    benefit == "Disability Support Pension" ~ "Disability support",
    benefit == "Mobility Allowance"         ~ "Disability support",
    #
    benefit == "Dad and Partner Pay"         ~ "Family and parenting",
    benefit == "Family Tax Benefits"         ~ "Family and parenting",
    benefit == "Paid Parental Leave Payment" ~ "Family and parenting",
    benefit == "Parenting Payment"           ~ "Family and parenting",
    #
    benefit == "Age Pension"     ~ "Older Australians",
    benefit == "Widow Allowance" ~ "Older Australians",
    #
    benefit == "Austudy/Abstudy"                  ~ "Work and study",
    benefit == "Newstart Allowance and Jobseeker" ~ "Work and study",
    benefit == "Youth Allowance"                  ~ "Work and study",
    #
    benefit == "Future Flexible Support Payment"          ~ "Other payments",
    benefit == "Special Benefit"                          ~ "Other payments",
    benefit == "Other government pensions and allowances" ~ "Other payments",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# Data wrangling
benefit_agesex <- benefit_agesex %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = benefit,
                          dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_total = aboriginal_n_carer_support + aboriginal_n_disability_support + 
                                   aboriginal_n_family_and_parenting + aboriginal_n_older_australians + 
                                   aboriginal_n_work_and_study + aboriginal_n_other_payments,
                #
                carer_prop      = aboriginal_n_carer_support / aboriginal_total * 100,
                disability_prop = aboriginal_n_disability_support / aboriginal_total * 100,
                family_prop     = aboriginal_n_family_and_parenting / aboriginal_total * 100,
                older_prop      = aboriginal_n_older_australians / aboriginal_total * 100,
                study_prop      = aboriginal_n_work_and_study / aboriginal_total * 100,
                other_prop      = aboriginal_n_other_payments / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.na(.), 0)),
                across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.nan(.), 0))) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(age_group,
                sex,
                carer_n = aboriginal_n_carer_support,
                carer_prop,
                disability_n = aboriginal_n_disability_support,
                disability_prop,
                family_n = aboriginal_n_family_and_parenting,
                family_prop,
                older_n = aboriginal_n_older_australians,
                older_prop,
                study_n = aboriginal_n_work_and_study,
                study_prop,
                other_n = aboriginal_n_other_payments,
                other_prop,
                aboriginal_total)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census) linked to data from the Australian Taxation Office and Department of Social Services held in the [Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)](https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida).

- The most common main types of income support payment received by people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were work and study (48%, n = 1,814), family and parenting (20%, n = 741), and disability support (16%, n = 611).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census and who were receiving a work and study support payment ranged from 308 (Darebin and Whittlesea LGAs) to 30 (Manningham LGA).

- Of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census and who were receiving income support, the percentage who were receiving a work and study support payment ranged from 67% (Boroondara LGA) to 42% (Banyule and Nillumbik LGAs).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census and who were receiving a family and parenting support payment ranged from 183 (Whittlesea LGA) to 10 (Boroondara LGA).

- Of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census and who were receiving income support, the percentage who were receiving a family and parenting support payment ranged from 27% (Whittlesea LGA) to 6.5% (Yarra LGA).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census and who were receiving a disability support payment ranged from 99 (Darebin and Hume LGAs) to 10 (Nillumbik and Manningham LGAs).

- Of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census and who were receiving income support, the percentage who were receiving a disability support payment ranged from 19% (Banyule LGA) to 12% (Boroondara LGA).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultations during the development of this report it was mentioned that people often encounter barriers when trying to access income support payments.

::: {.callout-note title="Data notes" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census) linked to data from the Australian Taxation Office and Department of Social Services held in the [Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)](https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida). Data are publicly available at Local Government Area (LGA), ABS Statistical Area Level 2 (SA2), and Indigenous Area of Residence (IARE) level.
  - PLIDA is a secure linked data asset maintained by the ABS that brings together information on health, education, government payments, income and taxation, employment, and population demographics.
  - The 2021 Census was held on the evening of August 10th 2021.
  - Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples were defined as those who identified themselves as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census.

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- The types of income support payments were classified as:
  - Carer support (Carer Allowance, Carer Payment)
  - Disability support (Disability Support Pension, Mobility Allowance)
  - Family and parenting (Dad and Partner Pay, Family Tax Benefits, Paid Parental Leave Payment, Parenting Payment)
  - Older Australians (Age Pension, Widow Allowance)
  - Work and study (Austudy/Abstudy, Newstart Allowance and Jobseeker, Youth Allowance)
  - Other payments (Future Flexible Support Payment, Special Benefit, other government pensions and allowances)

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- This indicator measures the main type of income support payment received. People may have received more than one type of income support payment.

- A number of regions across the state were in various stages of lockdown during the 2020/2021 financial year. This resulted in a greater number of people being stood down from work than usual, which may have had an impact on the receipt of income support payments.
:::

## Financial Security

### Basic Living Expenses

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic living expenses
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
financial_expenses <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Financial_LivingExpenses.csv")

# Data wrangling
financial_expenses <- financial_expenses %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(had_days_without_money_for_basic_living_expenses_in_last_12_months_n:did_not_have_days_without_money_for_basic_living_expenses_in_last_12_months_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(withoutyes_n = had_days_without_money_for_basic_living_expenses_in_last_12_months_n,
                withoutno_n  = did_not_have_days_without_money_for_basic_living_expenses_in_last_12_months_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(withoutyes_n:withoutno_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("withoutyes"),
                starts_with("withoutno"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>%
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
    #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "withoutyes" = "Yes",
                                              "withoutno"  = "No",
                                              "answered"   = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 43% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they had at least one day during the previous 12 months where they did not have money for basic living expenses (clothing or bills). This equates to approximately 16,400 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to report having at least one day where they did not have money for basic living expenses (clothing or bills) than males (49% vs. 38%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of a representative for each household completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- In the last 12 months were there any days when you or other people in your household ran out of money for clothing or bills?
  - Yes
  - No

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

:::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Table 6E-4

::: {#tab_6E_4 .fig-tab-title}
**Table 6E-4:** Whether had days without money for basic living expenses (clothing or bills) during the previous 12 months for people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, Greater Melbourne, by sex, 2022-2023
:::

```{r}
#
table_count  <- table_count + 1
table_number <- paste0("Table_", table_section, "_", sprintf("%.02d", table_count))

table <- financial_expenses %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = "sex",
                     values_from = c("n", "prop"),
                     names_vary  = "slowest") %>% 
  #
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(days_without_money = answer)

if (!file.exists(paste0(here::here(), "/data/", table_number, ".csv"))) {
  
  write.csv(table, paste0(here::here(), "/data/", table_number, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  
}

table %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(prop_male   = sprintf("%.1f", prop_male),
                prop_female = sprintf("%.1f", prop_female),
                prop_total  = sprintf("%.1f", prop_total)) %>%
  #
  f_table_grouped_sex(n_variable  = "estimate",
                      column_name = "Days without money<br>for basic expenses")
```

### Emergency Funds

```{r}

financial_emergency <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Financial_Emergency.csv")

  #

                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>%
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 61% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that their household would be able to raise $2,000 in a week during an emergency. This equates to approximately 23,200 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to report that their household would be able to raise emergency funds than males (64% vs. 58%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}

  - Don't know

### Food Security

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Food security
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
financial_foodsecurity <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Financial_FoodSecurity.csv")

# Data wrangling
financial_foodsecurity <- financial_foodsecurity %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(food_secure_n:severely_food_insecure_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(secure_n   = food_secure_n,
                marginal_n = marginally_food_insecure_n,
                moderate_n = moderately_food_insecure_n,
                severe_n   = severely_food_insecure_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(secure_n:severe_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("secure"),
                starts_with("marginal"),
                starts_with("moderate"),
                starts_with("severe"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "secure"   = "Food secure",
                                              "marginal" = "Marginal insecurity",
                                              "moderate" = "Moderate insecurity",
                                              "severe"   = "Severe insecurity",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Food secure", 
                                           "Marginal insecurity", 
                                           "Moderate insecurity", 
                                           "Severe insecurity",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 59% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they were food secure at all times during the previous 12 months. This equates to approximately 22,900 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males were more likely to report being food secure than females (62% vs. 55%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of a representative for each household completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- In the last 12 months, how often did you or other people in your household worry about whether food would run out before you got money to buy more?
  - Often
  - Sometimes
  - Never
  - Don't know

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 12 months, how often was the food that you bought not enough for everyone in the household and you didn't have money to buy more??
  - Often
  - Sometimes
  - Never
  - Don't know
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the last 12 months, how often were you or other people in your household not able to afford to eat healthy or nutritious meals?
  - Often
  - Sometimes
  - Never
  - Don't know
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

If at least one of these questions was answered in the affirmative (often or sometimes), additional questions were asked to determine the level of food insecurity (marginal, moderate, or severe).

- In the last 12 months, did you or other adults in your household ever have to eat smaller meals than usual or skip meals because there wasn't enough money for food?
- If yes, how often did this happen?
- In the last 12 months, did you ever eat less than you felt you should because there was not enough money for food?
- In the last 12 months, were you ever hungry but didn't eat because there wasn't enough money for food?
- In the last 12 months, did you lose weight without trying to because there wasn't enough money to buy food?
- In the last 12 months, did you or other adults in your household not eat for a whole day because there wasn't enough money for food?
- If yes, how often did this happen?

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Food security is defined as having enough food and/or money to buy food needed for an active, healthy life at all times during the previous 12 months.
  - Marginal food insecurity is generally characterised by worrying about running out of food or experiencing a lack of selection of food due to a lack of money for food.
  - Moderate food insecurity is generally characterised by compromising on the quality and/or quantity of food due to a lack of money for food.
  - Severe food insecurity is generally characterised by missing meals or reducing food intake due to a lack of money for food.
  
<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::
